---
title: "03 — PCA for predictor structure and model context"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** predictor-space variation, which survey categories shape the principal components, and how the encoded structure relates descriptively to frequent mental distress. PCA does not identify causal drivers, rank predictive importance, or classify Indigenous populations. This analysis uses 2014–2022 development records only.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}

load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## 1. Fit development-only PCA

**What this measures:** How much of the variation in encoded survey predictors can be summarized by principal components. The original training set is intentionally enriched with AI/AN respondents; the scatterplot should not be interpreted as a population-representative map. The analysis never uses FMD or race to construct the components.

```{r fit-exploratory-pca, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit unsupervised PCA on a bounded development sample
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Use the same prepared data and encodings as the classifiers.
# Outcomes and race classifications are excluded from the PCA matrix.
check_packages(c("data.table", "Matrix", "ggplot2", "scales"))
# Prefer the active run. If it only contains later analysis stages, reuse the
# most recent earlier development checkpoint without retraining anything.
active_checkpoint <- artifact_path("checkpoints", "02_development")

if (file.exists(active_checkpoint)) {
    development_checkpoint <- active_checkpoint
} else {
    run_directories <- list.dirs(
        file.path(project_root, "outputs"),
        recursive = FALSE,
        full.names = TRUE
    )
    run_directories <- run_directories[
        grepl("^run_[0-9]+$", basename(run_directories))
    ]
    run_ids <- sub("^run_", "", basename(run_directories))
    candidate_files <- file.path(
        run_directories,
        "checkpoints",
        sprintf("02_development_run_%s.rds", run_ids)
    )
    candidates <- candidate_files[file.exists(candidate_files)]
    candidate_ids <- as.integer(run_ids[file.exists(candidate_files)])

    if (!length(candidates)) {
        stop("No prior 02_development checkpoint exists. Run notebook 02 first.")
    }
    development_checkpoint <- candidates[which.max(candidate_ids)]
}

cat("[PCA] Reading frozen development sample:", development_checkpoint, "\n")
training <- readRDS(development_checkpoint)

set.seed(seed + 3L)
selected <- sample.int(
    nrow(training),
    size = min(nrow(training), max_pca_rows)
)
sample_data <- data.table::as.data.table(training[selected])

# Convert the survey predictors to numeric indicator columns.
encoded <- as.matrix(matrix_inputs(sample_data))
column_sd <- apply(encoded, 2, stats::sd)
retain <- is.finite(column_sd) & column_sd > 0
encoded <- encoded[, retain, drop = FALSE]

if (ncol(encoded) < 2L) {
    stop("At least two varying encoded predictors are required for PCA")
}

# Standardizing each indicator puts all columns on an equal SD scale.
# Rare categories can receive disproportionate influence, so loadings
# and missing-value categories must be inspected before interpretation.
pca <- stats::prcomp(
    encoded,
    center = TRUE,
    scale. = TRUE
)

explained <- pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)
variance_table <- data.frame(
    component = seq_along(explained),
    explained_fraction = explained,
    cumulative_fraction = cumsum(explained)
)

save_table(variance_table, "03b_pca_variance")
cat(sprintf(
    "[PCA] PC1 and PC2 jointly explain %.1f%% of encoded predictor variation.\n",
    100 * sum(explained[1:2])
))
print(utils::head(variance_table, 10))

# Show how quickly the principal components capture variation.
scree_data <- utils::head(variance_table, 12)
scree_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    scree_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = component, y = explained_fraction)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = atg_palette[["gold"]], width = 0.75) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = scree_data$component) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "How much predictor variation does PCA capture?",
        subtitle = "Development records, 2014–2022; PCA uses encoded predictors only",
        x = "Principal component",
        y = "Share of encoded predictor variation",
        caption = paste(
            "Low explained variance in PC1 and PC2 means their scatterplot",
            "cannot summarize the full predictor space."
        )
    )

show_and_save(scree_plot, "03b_pca_explained_variance", 10, 5)
```

## 2. Identify which categories define PC1 and PC2

**What this measures:** The signed *loadings* on the first two axes. These are not causal effects or machine learning feature importance. One-hot encoded categories (especially rare and `Missing` levels) can strongly influence standardized PCA.

```{r interpret-pca-loadings, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Examine principal component loadings
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

loadings <- data.table::as.data.table(
    pca$rotation[, 1:2, drop = FALSE],
    keep.rownames = "encoded_feature"
)

loadings_long <- data.table::melt(
    loadings,
    id.vars = "encoded_feature",
    variable.name = "component",
    value.name = "loading"
)
loadings_long[, absolute_loading := abs(loading)]

# Save all loadings for auditability, not just the displayed subset.
save_table(loadings_long, "03b_pca_feature_loadings")

# Select the eight largest absolute loadings for each component.
top_loadings <- loadings_long[
    order(-absolute_loading),
    utils::head(.SD, 8L),
    by = component
]

# Show the signed contribution of each encoded response category.
loadings_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    top_loadings,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = stats::reorder(encoded_feature, loading),
        y = loading,
        fill = component
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~component, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            PC1 = atg_palette[["rust"]],
            PC2 = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]
        )
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none") +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Which survey responses shape the PCA axes?",
        subtitle = "Eight largest absolute loadings per component",
        x = "Encoded survey response category",
        y = "Signed component loading",
        caption = "Loadings describe predictor variation, not predictive importance or causation."
    )

show_and_save(loadings_plot, "03b_pca_loading_contributions", 11, 6)
print(top_loadings)
```

## 3. Examine population overlap in the projected sample

**What this measures:** Where sampled development respondents appear on the first two PCA axes. The training sample is deliberately not representative of the national race distribution. Visual overlap does **not** establish equal model performance or absence of structural differences.

```{r show-pca-score-scatter, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize development respondents in PCA space
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

scores <- data.table::data.table(
    pc1 = pca$x[, 1],
    pc2 = pca$x[, 2],
    YEAR = sample_data$YEAR,
    cohort = sample_data$cohort,
    FMD = sample_data$FMD,
    train_weight = sample_data$train_weight
)

scatter_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    scores,
    ggplot2::aes(x = pc1, y = pc2, color = cohort)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.27, size = 0.7) +
    atg_scale_color_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Exploratory distribution of survey predictors",
        subtitle = sprintf(
            "PC1 and PC2 capture %.1f%% of variation in this development sample",
            100 * sum(explained[1:2])
        ),
        x = "Principal component 1",
        y = "Principal component 2",
        color = "Race classification",
        caption = paste(
            "AI/AN-enriched computational sample; not nationally representative.",
            "Axes are defined without using FMD or race."
        )
    )

show_and_save(scatter_plot, "03b_pca_scatter", 10, 6)
```

## 4. Does the PCA structure correspond to reported distress?

**What this measures:** Weighted FMD prevalence across ten ordered groups of PC1 scores in the 2014–2022 development sample. This is a *descriptive association check*, not a new classifier, a predictor ranking, or a fair evaluation on held-out survey years. No confidence intervals are shown; this is exploratory only.

```{r check-pca-outcome-signal, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compare FMD prevalence across PC1-score groups
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rank respondents by PC1 so each ordered bin contains a similar
# number of development records. Respondents may share a score.
scores[, pc1_rank := data.table::frank(pc1, ties.method = "average")]
scores[
    ,
    pc1_decile := pmax(
        1L,
        pmin(10L, as.integer(ceiling(10 * pc1_rank / .N)))
    )
]

# Compensate for computational subsampling using existing training
# weights, then compare the two primary populations descriptively.
pc1_distress <- scores[
    cohort %in% primary_groups &
        FMD %in% c(0, 1) &
        valid_weight(train_weight),
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        fmd_prevalence = weighted_mean(FMD, train_weight)
    ),
    by = .(pc1_decile, cohort)
][order(pc1_decile, cohort)]

save_table(pc1_distress, "03b_pca_pc1_distress_association")

outcome_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    pc1_distress,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = pc1_decile,
        y = fmd_prevalence,
        color = cohort,
        group = cohort
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
    ) +
    atg_scale_color_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Does PC1 capture variation associated with mental distress?",
        subtitle = "Development sample, 2014–2022; survey/subsampling-weighted descriptive rates",
        x = "PC1 score group (lowest to highest)",
        y = "Reported frequent mental distress",
        color = "Population",
        caption = paste(
            "Exploratory association only. PC1 was not optimized for FMD.",
            "No design-based confidence intervals are estimated here."
        )
    )

show_and_save(outcome_plot, "03b_pca_pc1_distress", 10, 5)
print(pc1_distress)
```

## 5. Check whether the PCA profile shifts across development years

**What this measures:** Whether the *weighted average PC1 score* changes from 2014 through 2022 within each population. This is an exploratory check of changing predictor composition, not a formal test of temporal model drift or a forecast. The PCA basis is fitted once on development records and remains fixed across these years.

```{r check-pca-year-shift, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Check changes in principal component scores across development years
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Use the computational-sampling-adjusted training weights to describe
# the average PCA score in each year and population. These estimates
# remain exploratory and have no design-based uncertainty intervals.
yearly_pc1 <- scores[
    cohort %in% primary_groups & valid_weight(train_weight),
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        mean_pc1 = weighted_mean(pc1, train_weight)
    ),
    by = .(YEAR, cohort)
][order(YEAR, cohort)]

save_table(yearly_pc1, "03b_pca_annual_pc1_shift")

year_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    yearly_pc1,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = YEAR,
        y = mean_pc1,
        color = cohort,
        group = cohort
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        linewidth = 0.5,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = development_years) +
    atg_scale_color_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Do survey predictor profiles shift across development years?",
        subtitle = "Annual weighted mean PC1 score, using a fixed 2014–2022 PCA basis",
        x = "BRFSS survey year",
        y = "Average PC1 score (standardized PCA units)",
        color = "Population",
        caption = paste(
            "Exploratory computational sample; no survey-design CIs.",
            "A change in PC1 is not necessarily a change in predictive accuracy."
        )
    )

show_and_save(year_plot, "03b_pca_annual_pc1_profile", 11, 5)
print(yearly_pc1)
```

## Interpretation and next step

- PCA is **unsupervised**. Its axes cannot be used as evidence that a survey variable predicts FMD better than another.
- Inspect loadings before naming or interpreting PC1/PC2. A strong `Missing` loading may identify response patterns rather than a health dimension.
- The PCA scatterplot shows a deliberately AI/AN-enriched training sample and only two axes. It cannot measure national representativeness or establish model equity.
- Treat the annual-PC1 chart as an exploratory composition signal, not proof of model drift. Use `11_Annual_Shifts.Rmd` and `15_Predictor_Changes_Across_Years.Rmd` for stronger time-shift and predictive-relevance analyses, and the later AI/AN evaluation for held-out model performance.
- For predominantly categorical predictors, multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) may be more natural than standardized dummy-variable PCA; this PCA is retained to meet your class foundation.
